Cc: BetaCorp Billing <billing@betacorp.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Elevated latency impacting Checkout - urgent compensation discussion

Kimberly,

We experienced sustained elevated P99 latency on your hosted inference endpoint (redwood-prod-cc-03) between 02:40 and 05:15 PDT on 2026-09-22. This impacted our checkout path and caused multiple failed tokenizations in our payment flow. Our engineering team measured ~180% increase in average tail latency and a visible rise in error retries.

This had direct revenue impact (we estimate ~1.8% drop in conversion during the window). Per our contract SLOs (99.9% uptime, P99 <= 600ms), this looks like a clear breach. We need to understand remediation and request a commercial remediation proposal (credit and a short-term change to routing to reduce recurrence).

Attached: incident-log-export (truncated) and a short damage estimate for Q3 revenue implications. Please escalate — we expect a written proposal by end of day tomorrow.

Thanks,
Sam O'Neill
Director of Engineering, BetaCorp
sam.oneill@betacorp.com

Subject: Re: Elevated latency impacting Checkout - urgent compensation discussion

Aditya / Karthik — forwarding BetaCorp's note. They reported a P99 latency and conversion impact for a 2.5h window on 9/22. I pulled an initial analysis (attached) and the ops timeline. Summary: batch sizing regression plus a routing backoff produced the tail increase; short-term mitigation rolled by 03:05 and full normalization by 05:30.

Recommended commercial offer (initial):
- 20% credit on September hosted consumption invoice for their impacted Dedicated pool (amortized across the month)
- One complimentary month of reserved capacity credit (applied at renewal)
- Technical follow-up: free performance tuning session with our runtime team and a dedicated routing rule for their critical checkout route for 90 days

Rationale: Keeps them whole on unit economics, demonstrates goodwill, and adds a low-cost engineering deliverable that reduces recurrence risk. Estimated financial exposure for Redwood: ~$28k (credit + month subsidy). This is above standard rep authority; requesting exec signoff from Marissa for anything >$25k.

Attachments: slo-impact-analysis-sep2026.xlsx, incident-report-betacorp-20260923.pdf

Kimberly Park
Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Kimberly — quick thoughts from GTM/pricing perspective:
- 20% credit + one free month is reasonable and aligns with similar remediation we offered in Q2 to two enterprise customers.
- Recommend we structure as a formal credit memo, split: 15% invoice credit for Sep consumption + $15k one-time service credit (applied as invoice line item) rather than a free month, unless legal prefers a month.
- If we convert the free month into a fixed $ value we can keep exposure capped; my estimate for a month of their Dedicated pool = ~$22k, so combined exposure would be ~ $37k.

Approval runway: anything over $35k needs Marissa + FP&A sign-off per policy. If we keep to $35k or less we can approve quickly.

I recommend proposing the following to BetaCorp in one document: 15% consumption credit for Sep (amortized), + $20k service credit (applied as a billing line) + technical follow-up deliverables. That keeps us just under $35k and looks stronger than 15% alone.

- Aditya
